title: Devotion and patience
intro: Islam means giving ourselves fully to Allah – and patience (sabr) is the believer’s weapon through life’s tests.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Say: “My prayer, my worship, my life and my death are truly for Allah, Lord of the worlds.” <small>(Qur’an, Al-An‘am 6:162)</small>

learn.label: Qur’an, Al-An‘am 6:162
learn.ar: قُلْ إِنَّ صَلَاتِي وَنُسُكِي وَمَحْيَايَ وَمَمَاتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
learn.tr: Qul inna salaatee wa nusukee wa mahyaaya wa mamaatee lillaahi Rabbil-‘aalameen
learn.en: Say: “My prayer, my worship, my life and my death are for Allah, Lord of the worlds.”

learn.html: The religion Allah (SWT) revealed from Adam (AS) to Muhammad (SAW) is called Islam. Islam means complete devotion, obedience and humility to Allah, without any resistance, shown through faith, doing the Islamic duties and good behaviour.

The main aim of Islam is to turn people away from worshipping created things, idols and desires, and to direct them to worship, obey and be devoted only to Allah – until love for Him is born and settles in a Muslim’s heart.
All our activities and our whole life are devotion to Allah (SWT) if:

items: they are in line with Allah’s law,
our heart is filled with taqwa, and
our final aim is to reach Allah’s pleasure.

learn.html: A Muslim draws spiritually closer to Allah not only through Salah but through all their everyday activities. They can only do this if they are steadfast and patient.

Patience (sabr) is bearing life’s troubles and hardships with dignity and courage, and not falling into fear and worry when misfortunes and accidents happen. Patience is the Muslim’s weapon in the struggle through life and its tests.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: When asked which people are tested most, Muhammad (SAW) answered: “The prophets of Allah, then the best, then the next best. A person is tested according to his faith: if his faith is strong, his tests are greater; if his faith is weak, his tests are smaller. A person will be tested until he walks on the earth completely free of sin.” (Tirmidhi)

learn.title: 1. Patience in obedience
learn.html: Being steadfast in doing good deeds and acts of worship. This kind of patience needs true ikhlas – sincerity to Allah (SWT) in our intention, which removes showing off (hypocrisy).

learn.title: 2. Patience in hardship
learn.html: Patiently bearing everything Allah (SWT) has decreed for a person.

learn.title: 3. Patience with people
learn.html: Staying firm when people hurt us or treat us badly. Muhammad (SAW) said: “The believer who mixes with people and patiently bears their harm has a greater reward than the believer who does not mix with them and does not bear their harm.” (Ahmad)

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “How wonderful is the affair of the believer – everything that happens to him is good, and this is only for the believer. If something good happens to him, he is thankful, and that is good for him; if something bad happens to him, he is patient, and that is good for him.” (Muslim)
In the Qur’an Allah (SWT) tells us about three joys that await the patient for their patience in hardship (Qur’an, Al-Baqarah 2:155–157):

items.label: Allah will have mercy on them
They are surely on the right path

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: When you see where you are weak at keeping your patience, try to push your limits and be more patient – you will be rewarded for it.

practice.title: Which kind of patience?
practice.prompt: Sort each example into the right kind of patience.

items.text: Getting up for Fajr on a cold winter morning
Fasting on a long summer day in Ramadan
Going to maktab every week, even when tired
Staying calm when you are ill for a long time
Not losing hope when you lose something precious
Not answering back when a classmate teases you
Waiting kindly for a slow little brother

practice.title: Devotion to Allah
practice.prompt: Tap the three things that make all our activities devotion to Allah, then tap Check.

options.text: 📜 They are in line with Allah’s law
❤️ Our heart is full of taqwa
👏 Other people praise us for them
options.why: Doing things for people’s praise is showing off – devotion is only for Allah.

options.text: 🏆 We do them better than everyone else
options.why: Devotion is not a competition – it is about following Allah’s law with taqwa, for His pleasure.

questions.q: What does the word Islam mean?
options: Complete devotion and obedience to Allah
Bearing hardships with dignity and courage
The prophets, then the best people

questions.q: Which kind of patience needs true ikhlas?
options: Patience in waiting for a bus

questions.q: Who has a greater reward, according to the hadith in Ahmad?
options: The believer who mixes with people and bears their harm patiently
The one who stays away from everyone

questions.q: What does a believer do when something good happens?
Which is NOT one of the three joys promised to the patient?

practice.title: Questions and tasks
prompts: 💬 How is devotion to Allah (SWT) shown? What is patience? What are the kinds of patience? How does Allah (SWT) reward patience?
🤲 Choose a task (1): Describe a situation in your life when you showed special devotion to Allah (SWT).
💪 Choose a task (2): Remember a situation in your life that needed a lot of patience from you. Share it with your classmates!
